2018). The eight natural vitamin E analogs and also synthetic all-rac-aT are taken up across the intestinal epithelium with similar
efﬁciency ranging from 10 to 80%. Distribution to peripheral cells of these vitamin E analogs coming from the intestine is mediated
by chylomicrons (and in part also from high density lipoproteins (HDL)), and chylomicron remnants bring the remainder to the
liver. In the liver, aT (preferentially RRR, but less also RSR, RRS and RSS-side chain isomers, the so-called 2R-aT-stereoisomers
(Fig. 3)) are recognized by aTTP, retained and incorporated into VLDL, leading to an up to 50 fold enrichment of aT in plasma.
Fig. 4
Uptake, distribution, metabolism and secretion of different natural and synthetic vitamin E analogs and the most important genes involved. The
eight natural vitamin E analogs (aT, bT, gT, dT and aTT, bTT, gTT, dTT) are present in the diet in different quantities, and upon formation of mixed
micelles are absorbed by the intestine with similar efﬁciency. Intestinal and pancreatic esterases convert the stabilized vitamin E form (aTA) present as
precursor in many supplements into aT before it can be taken up by the intestine. Transport of the eight vitamin E analogs across the intestinal
